page: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor utilizing x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory provisioning is set at 64.0 GB, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A 322 GB local solid-state drive is directly attached for temporary scratch and cache storage, while graphical processing units are absent.

Benchmark results place the processor and memory subsystem consistently within average performance tiers. The system achieved a PassMark CPU score of 11541.37 alongside a Geekbench multi-core rating of 6145.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 62.3 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 44.14 GB/sec for large write operations. In operational workloads, the instance delivered 7.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.5 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference is limited, measuring 17.36 tokens per second for prompt processing and 6.39 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B parameter model.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides effective resource density for memory-bound applications without necessitating over-provisioned compute cores. Because local storage is included as temporary SSD space, persistent deployments require attached remote managed disks. The hardware profile is appropriate for in-memory caching layers, relational databases, enterprise resource planning backends, and moderate data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores of a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM. The instance incorporates an x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 vector support and includes 322 GB of local temporary SSD storage, with no GPU hardware present. Benchmarks show balanced throughput, producing 7.88 million Redis SET operations per second, 12.5 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6145.0. Its 8 GB per vCPU allocation enables cost-efficient memory scaling without excessive compute overhead, though large LLM inference remains constrained by the lack of accelerators. The instance fits in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data processing tasks requiring substantial working memory.
